# How GRACE Follow-On Uses Satellite Separation to Investigate Water Movement

GRACE Follow-On consists of two satellites that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. As they pass a larger concentration of mass, gravity affects the leading satellite first, initially increasing its distance from the trailing satellite.

Scientists use changes in the satellites’ separation to infer shifts in mass. Those inferred shifts help investigate changes in Earth’s water, including groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, glaciers and ice sheets, and sea level changes attributable to water added to the oceans.
